Date: Fri, 6 Jul 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Capacity contention: Lighthouse AI & KiteWorks commitments

Folks,

We have a live contention between two committed deals in us-west that requires an allocation decision this week. Summary: Lighthouse AI (enterprise, security-sensitive) has signed a term sheet for Dedicated with an initial need of ~120 A100-class GPUs pinned to their private pool; KiteWorks (mid-enterprise) has a signed commitment for 80 GPUs in same region starting next month. Our available A100-class equivalent pool in us-west is ~100 GPUs for the timeframe in question (after previously allocated reserved capacity).

Attachments: capacity_snapshot_20280706.csv, Lighthouse_SOW_v2.pdf, KiteWorks_commit_letter.pdf

Immediate asks:
- I need a short recommendation (prefer/compromise) by EOD today so we can reply to both customers and lock provisioning windows.
- Please call out operational risk, reconfig time, and any customer concessions we'd need to offer.

Notes to consider (quick):
- Lighthouse is asking for strict physical isolation and A100-class hardware for model parity with their on-prem. They represent ~3x ARR vs KiteWorks.
- KiteWorks has a firm start date and has referenced financial penalties in their T&Cs if we miss the first-month SLA.
- We can mix hardware and use routing + quant profiles, but Lighthouse insists on homogeneous A100 fleet for their validation.

Suggested framing for the reply to customers: phased onboarding for Lighthouse (partial A100 tranche now + staged increase) and a guaranteed baseline for KiteWorks with burst access and credits. But I want operations and infra to confirm feasibility before I send anything externally.

-Naomi
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

Why: ARR and strategic value (enterprise security play) + likelihood of expansion into Dedicated across additional regions. We should offer KiteWorks a commercially attractive alternative (guaranteed 60 GPUs on A10/A40-class with a documented burst window into A100s during night hours) plus a one-off credit for the first month to cover the SLA risk. That keeps KiteWorks whole from a contract perspective while protecting the long-term strategic revenue.

Operational caveats: confirm with infra whether we can carve a 60/40 split of A100s now and convert units over 4–6 weeks. If we can't, propose a phased delivery schedule in writing and push KiteWorks’ go-live 14 days with a credit for delay.

Quick technical reality check and a potential lever: of the ~100 GPUs available that are A100-equivalent, only ~60 are pure A100 class (NVLink + required ECO) and the remaining 40 are A100-lite / A10G-ish nodes. Lighthouse has validated models on NVLink topology and is firm that A100 homogeneity matters for their accuracy checks.

Operational levers we can use:
- Hardware partitioning: allocate the 60 pure A100s to Lighthouse immediately and promise the remaining A100-equivalent capacity over a staged window (30 units over 4–6 weeks) while giving KiteWorks guaranteed A10G-class capacity.
- Routing variant: serve KiteWorks on a quantized model variant (Q4/Q5) for cost/latency parity and route higher-quality requests to A100 when available.
- Temporary cross-region spill: we have ~20 spare A100s in us-east that could be used as burst capacity for Lighthouse for a short period while we reconfigure in us-west (network egress and latency caveats).

Markus — can you confirm reconfiguration time if we elect to move 30 nodes from A10G pool into A100-class (software-level affinity changes + kernel tuning), and whether that introduces a 24–72h window where latency will spike for existing customers?

-Vivek
Principal SRE
Redwood Inference

I can confirm the following after a quick pass with infra on-call:
- Reconfiguring a node from the A10G pool to an A100-class configuration (tuning kernels, enabling NVLink topologies, re-imaging if necessary) is a 48–72 hour operation per tranche when planned. If we parallelize across squads we can compress to ~36–48 hours but risk transient IO congestion on the storage fabric.
- Soft partitioning into dedicated node pools is feasible and is the safest operational approach — reduces blast radius, easier rollback.
- Cross-region spill to us-east is technically feasible for short bursts but will add 40–120ms tail latency (not suitable for Lighthouse’s SLOs), so only acceptable as temporary ramp.

I'll update the runbook: https://docs.redwood.com/runbooks/node-reconfig.md and can schedule the reconfig work if product/ops greenlights.

—Markus
VP, Infrastructure
Redwood Inference

Hi Asha / Jordan / Tom —

Thanks for your patience while we finalize a provisioning plan. To be transparent: we are constrained in us-west for A100-class hardware in the short window. We propose the following compromise to keep both programs on track:

1) Lighthouse AI: Immediate allocation of 60 A100 GPUs for validation day 1, plus an additional 30 A100 GPUs over the next 6 weeks (scheduled ramp). We will provide an isolated node pool and NVLink topology for those initial units.

2) KiteWorks: Guaranteed 60 GPUs on A10/A40-class nodes available at go-live, plus burstable access to remaining A100s during night windows (subject to availability). Redwood will provide a one-time credit equivalent to 5% of the first-month invoice if we miss the first-month SLA.

3) Ops notes: full parity (all 120 A100s) for Lighthouse will be delivered within 6 weeks; reconfiguration window may cause brief tail-latency increases which we will communicate in advance.

Please respond with acceptance or counter-proposals by COB Monday.

Best —
Ben
